question.text:
A finite group has order 60 and center of order 5. How many distinct inner automorphisms does
it have?
(A) 5 (B) 10 (C) 12 (D) 15 (E) 60

solution.text:
Two elements induce the same conjugation map exactly when they differ by a central
element. Hence the number of maps is |G|/|Z(G)| = 60/5 = 12.

question.text:
What is the order of the automorphism f (x) = 5x of the additive group Z ?
24
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 8

solution.text:
The multiplier 5 is a unit modulo 24, so the map is an automorphism. Its square is mul-
tiplication by 25 ≡ 1 (mod 24), but it is not itself the identity. Its order is therefore
two.

question.text:
Let V = Z × Z . What is the ordered pair (| Aut(V )|, | Inn(V )|)?
2 2
(A) (1, 1) (B) (3, 1) (C) (6, 1) (D) (6, 3) (E) (6, 6)

solution.text:
An automorphism permutes the three nonzero elements. Any such permutation preserves
addition: each nonzero element added to itself is zero, and the sum of two distinct nonzero
elements is the third. Thus all 3! = 6 permutations work. Since V is Abelian, every inner
automorphism is the identity.

question.text:
A group G has no automorphism other than the identity. Which statement must be true?
(A) G has exactly one element.
(B) G is infinite.
(C) G is non-Abelian.
